pass_condition: The four round-1 survivors are killed and the round-2 fixes are each defended by a test.

findings.statement: Mutant N1 survives: moving the transaction boundary so repositories commit before the params loop is unobserved, and under the new immutability rule that leaves a snapshot permanently un-completable.
findings.quoted_line: SURVIVED  N1  writer: transaction boundary moved (commit before the params loop)
findings.failure_scenario: With the boundary moved and a failure in the params loop: 'repositories rows COMMITTED: 3', 'params rows committed: 0', and the retry is refused forever -- 'retry PERMANENTLY BLOCKED: snapshot 'snap-1' already has repositories rows'. The suite reports 70 passed.

observations: 18 of 20 killed. All four round-1 survivors (M3 rank-on-unranked, M4 non-canonical JSON, M5 no commit, M10 unconditional rename) are now killed.

The three other new mutants aimed at round-2 fixes all die: N2 (legacy back in the include-list), N3 (immutability keyed on the wrong table), N4 (asdict dropped for one persona), plus N5/N6 (rollback dropped in migrations / in write_records).
M14 (ROW_NUMBER -> RANK) survives and is equivalent again: level 8 is lowercase owner/name, unique under UNIQUE(snapshot_id, owner, name).
__pycache__ cleared before every run; tree restored byte-identical after each mutant and at the end (git diff --stat empty).
The fix for N1 is a test, not code: assert that a params-loop failure leaves zero repositories rows for the snapshot.
